message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"67153205ff4a625f7a8daa0b302c77ac343e37b050b7f2b84ec4c99c7c3a9f27","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nc-class-c:lineage:78","source_registry_sha256":"e128656a3d00ba5437556728ebd87f5842c83601163739613417fe77cf9f423b","units":[{"unit_id":"sec14-u01","module_id":"sec14-m01","objective_ids":["sec14-u01"],"title":{"text":"Circular signals","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The handbook gives a clear meaning for each circular light, including when turns must yield.","fact_ids":["sec14-F02","sec14-F03","sec14-F05"]},{"text":"Turning right on red is allowed after a full stop unless signed, but you must yield, and failing to yield to a pedestrian carries a penalty.","fact_ids":["sec14-F05","sec14-F06","sec14-F07"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Avery stops at a steady red light and wants to turn right, with no sign forbidding it, while a pedestrian starts to cross in front of the stopped traffic.","fact_ids":["sec14-F05","sec14-F06"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A right turn on red is allowed after a complete stop unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted, but the driver must yield to pedestrians starting to cross nearby.","fact_ids":["sec14-F05","sec14-F06"]},"result":{"text":"Avery waits for the pedestrian to finish crossing before turning right.","fact_ids":["sec14-F06","sec14-F07"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: speeding up on a yellow light to get through before it turns red.","fact_ids":["sec14-F04"]},"correction":{"text":"Never speed up on a yellow light; stop unless you are too close to stop safely.","fact_ids":["sec14-F04","sec14-F03"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Stop unless too close.","fact_ids":["sec14-F03"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Avery is stopped at a red light, may turn right, and a pedestrian is starting to cross in front of the stopped traffic. What should Avery do?","fact_ids":["sec14-F06","sec14-F05"]},"answer":{"text":"Yield to the pedestrian before turning right.","fact_ids":["sec14-F06"]},"rationale":{"text":"Turning right on red requires yielding to traffic and to pedestrians in or entering the crossing.","fact_ids":["sec14-F06","sec14-F07"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec14-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Reading the lights","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03","sec14-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"What signals control.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03","sec14-F05"]},{"text":"Circular green, yellow and red.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03","sec14-F05"]},{"text":"Turning right on red.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03","sec14-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"This chapter covers traffic signals. It begins with the circular lights that most drivers see every day, then moves on to arrows, dark and flashing signals, flashing yellow arrows, ramp meters and hybrid beacons. In this first lesson you will review what traffic signals control, what a circular green allows and what turning drivers must do on green, how to handle a circular yellow, the rule against speeding up on yellow, what a steady red means, when you may turn right on red, whom you must yield to when you do, and the penalty for failing to yield to a pedestrian.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03","sec14-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Green and yellow","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Green: go straight or turn with caution.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03"]},{"text":"Turning drivers yield.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03"]},{"text":"Yellow: stop unless too close.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Traffic signals control both vehicles and pedestrians at some intersections and at some mid-block crosswalks. A circular green light lets you go straight or turn with caution, but turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. A circular yellow light warns that red is coming. Stop, unless you are too close to stop safely, in which case continue carefully through. So green allows movement but not priority for turns, and yellow is a warning to stop if you can do so safely. Neither light gives a turning driver the right to cut in front of oncoming traffic.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u01-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Never race the yellow","fact_ids":["sec14-F04","sec14-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Yellow warns that red is coming.","fact_ids":["sec14-F04","sec14-F03"]},{"text":"Never speed up to get through.","fact_ids":["sec14-F04","sec14-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some drivers treat yellow as a signal to speed up. The handbook says never speed up on a yellow light to try to get through before it turns red. A circular yellow light warns that red is coming, and the handbook's direction is to stop unless you are too close to stop safely, in which case you continue carefully. On practice questions, any option that suggests accelerating to get through before it turns red is wrong. The correct answers involve stopping when you can do so safely, or continuing carefully when you are already too close to stop.","fact_ids":["sec14-F04","sec14-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Steady red and right on red","fact_ids":["sec14-F05","sec14-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Steady red: stop.","fact_ids":["sec14-F05","sec14-F06"]},{"text":"Right on red after a full stop.","fact_ids":["sec14-F05","sec14-F06"]},{"text":"Unless NO TURN ON RED is posted.","fact_ids":["sec14-F05","sec14-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"A steady circular red means stop. You may then turn right after a complete stop, unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted. A driver turning right on red must yield to other traffic and to pedestrians in the intersection or starting to cross nearby in front of the stopped traffic. So a right turn on red has three conditions in the handbook: a complete stop first, no sign forbidding the turn, and yielding to both traffic and pedestrians. A rolling turn without a full stop, or a turn past a NO TURN ON RED sign, does not meet those conditions.","fact_ids":["sec14-F05","sec14-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The pedestrian penalty","fact_ids":["sec14-F07","sec14-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Failing to yield on right on red.","fact_ids":["sec14-F07","sec14-F06"]},{"text":"Penalty: one hundred to five hundred dollars.","fact_ids":["sec14-F07","sec14-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"Failing to yield to such a pedestrian while turning right on red carries a penalty of at least one hundred dollars and no more than five hundred dollars. The duty it backs up is the one from the last slide: a driver turning right on red must yield to other traffic and to pedestrians in the intersection or starting to cross nearby in front of the stopped traffic. So when you turn right on red, the pedestrians in the intersection and those starting to cross in front of the stopped traffic go first, and you complete the turn after them.","fact_ids":["sec14-F07","sec14-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the right on red","fact_ids":["sec14-F06","sec14-F05","sec14-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Stopped at a red light.","fact_ids":["sec14-F06","sec14-F05","sec14-F07"]},{"text":"A pedestrian starts to cross.","fact_ids":["sec14-F06","sec14-F05","sec14-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: Avery is stopped at a steady red light and wants to turn right. There is no NO TURN ON RED sign, but a pedestrian is starting to cross in front of the stopped traffic beside Avery. What should Avery do? Work it out before reading on. Avery should yield to the pedestrian before turning right. A driver turning right on red must yield to other traffic and to pedestrians in the intersection or starting to cross nearby. Failing to yield to that pedestrian carries a penalty of at least one hundred dollars and no more than five hundred dollars.","fact_ids":["sec14-F06","sec14-F05","sec14-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Circular signals recap","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03","sec14-F04","sec14-F05","sec14-F06","sec14-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Green: go, turners yield.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03","sec14-F04","sec14-F05","sec14-F06","sec14-F07"]},{"text":"Yellow: stop unless too close.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03","sec14-F04","sec14-F05","sec14-F06","sec14-F07"]},{"text":"Red: stop, right on red with care.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03","sec14-F04","sec14-F05","sec14-F06","sec14-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Let us recap. Traffic signals control vehicles and pedestrians at some intersections and mid-block crosswalks. A circular green lets you go straight or turn with caution, with turning drivers yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. A circular yellow warns that red is coming: stop unless you are too close, and never speed up to get through before it turns red. A steady circular red means stop, and you may turn right after a complete stop unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted, yielding to traffic and pedestrians. Failing to yield to a pedestrian there carries a penalty of one hundred to five hundred dollars.","fact_ids":["sec14-F01","sec14-F02","sec14-F03","sec14-F04","sec14-F05","sec14-F06","sec14-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec14-u02","module_id":"sec14-m02","objective_ids":["sec14-u02"],"title":{"text":"Arrow signals","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-R01","sec14-F09"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The handbook says arrows give or end protected movements, while circular lights give permitted ones.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-F11","sec14-R01"]},{"text":"When arrows and circular lights share a signal, each controls different traffic.","fact_ids":["sec14-F12","sec14-F13"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Lee is waiting to make a U-turn on a green arrow while a driver across the intersection turns right on a green arrow at the same time.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09"]},"reasoning":{"text":"When a U-turn and an opposing right turn both have green arrows at once, the U-turning driver yields to the right-turning driver.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-F08"]},"result":{"text":"Lee waits for the right-turning driver before making the U-turn.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: treating a circular green like a green arrow when turning left.","fact_ids":["sec14-R01"]},"correction":{"text":"A circular green lets you turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, while a green arrow gives you a protected turn.","fact_ids":["sec14-R01","sec14-F02","sec14-F08"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Circle yields, arrow protected.","fact_ids":["sec14-R01"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Lee has a green arrow for a U-turn while an opposing driver has a green arrow to turn right. Who yields?","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-F08"]},"answer":{"text":"Lee, the U-turning driver, yields.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09"]},"rationale":{"text":"When both movements have green arrows, the handbook makes the U-turning driver yield to the right-turning driver.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-R01"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec14-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Arrows and circles","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-F09","sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Green, red and yellow arrows.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-F09","sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},{"text":"U-turns on arrows.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-F09","sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},{"text":"When arrows and circles share a signal.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-F09","sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers arrow signals and how they differ from circular lights of the same color. You will review what a green arrow gives you, the special yield rule when a U-turn and an opposing right turn both have green arrows, what a red arrow means, what a yellow arrow warns about, and how arrows and circular lights divide control when they appear on the same signal. Each arrow color has a circular counterpart with a different meaning, and practice questions often test those differences, so as you go, compare each arrow with its matching circle.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-F09","sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Green arrows","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-F09","sec14-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"A protected movement.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-F09","sec14-R01"]},{"text":"Enter carefully in the arrow's direction.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-F09","sec14-R01"]},{"text":"Circular green turns must yield.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-F09","sec14-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"A green arrow gives a protected movement, allowing you to enter the intersection carefully in the direction the arrow points. When a U-turn and an opposing right turn both have green arrows at once, the U-turning driver yields to the right-turning driver. So a green arrow protects your turn from oncoming traffic, but the handbook still asks you to enter carefully, and it adds one specific yield rule for U-turns. By contrast, a circular green lets you turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, which is a permitted turn rather than a protected one.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-F09","sec14-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u02-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Circle or arrow for green","fact_ids":["sec14-R01","sec14-F02","sec14-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Circular green: yield before turning.","fact_ids":["sec14-R01","sec14-F02","sec14-F08"]},{"text":"Green arrow: protected turn.","fact_ids":["sec14-R01","sec14-F02","sec14-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. A circular green lets you turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, while a green arrow gives you a protected turn. Practice questions may describe a driver turning left on a circular green and suggest the driver has the right of way. That is wrong. On a circular green, the turning driver yields to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Only a green arrow makes the turn protected. When a question shows a green light, check its shape first, because the shape decides whether your turn is protected or must wait for a gap.","fact_ids":["sec14-R01","sec14-F02","sec14-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Red and yellow arrows","fact_ids":["sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Red arrow: turns that way must stop.","fact_ids":["sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},{"text":"Yellow arrow: protected phase ending.","fact_ids":["sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},{"text":"Changes to green, red or a red arrow.","fact_ids":["sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"A red arrow means drivers turning in that direction must stop. A yellow arrow warns that the protected green arrow is ending and will change to a circular green, a circular red or a red arrow. So a red arrow stops one movement, the turn it points to, and a yellow arrow announces that the protection for that turn is about to end. When the yellow arrow changes to a circular green, turns become permitted, meaning you yield. When it changes to a circular red or a red arrow, the turn must stop, as with any red. So a red arrow and a yellow arrow each control only the turn they point to.","fact_ids":["sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u02-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Red and yellow: circle or arrow","fact_ids":["sec14-R03","sec14-R02","sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Circular red: right after stopping, unless signed.","fact_ids":["sec14-R03","sec14-R02","sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},{"text":"Red arrow: no turn that way.","fact_ids":["sec14-R03","sec14-R02","sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},{"text":"Yellow arrow: protection ending.","fact_ids":["sec14-R03","sec14-R02","sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the second trap. A steady circular red still allows a right turn after a full stop unless signed otherwise, while a red arrow stops all turning traffic in that direction. And a circular yellow means stop if you safely can, while a yellow arrow means the protected arrow phase is about to end. Practice questions may treat a red arrow like a circular red and allow a right turn after stopping. They are not the same. A red arrow pointing right means no right turn until it changes. Check the shape of every red and yellow light.","fact_ids":["sec14-R03","sec14-R02","sec14-F10","sec14-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u02-s6","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Arrows with circular lights","fact_ids":["sec14-F12","sec14-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"No arrow lit: circles control everyone.","fact_ids":["sec14-F12","sec14-F13"]},{"text":"Both lit: arrows for turns, circles for through.","fact_ids":["sec14-F12","sec14-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Some signals combine protected arrows with unprotected circular lights. When no arrow is lit, circular lights control both through and turning traffic. When arrows and circular lights show together, the arrows control turning traffic and the circular lights control through traffic. So on a combined signal, look for an arrow first. If one is lit for your turn, follow it. If no arrow is lit, the circular light controls your turn as well as through traffic, which means a circular green turn must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.","fact_ids":["sec14-F12","sec14-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u02-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the U-turn arrow","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Lee has a green arrow for a U-turn.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-F08"]},{"text":"An opposing driver has a right-turn arrow.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: Lee is waiting to make a U-turn on a green arrow. At the same moment, a driver across the intersection has a green arrow to turn right, into the road Lee is about to use. Who yields? Work it out before reading on. Lee, the U-turning driver, yields. When a U-turn and an opposing right turn both have green arrows at once, the handbook says the U-turning driver yields to the right-turning driver. A green arrow still means entering carefully, and this is one case where a protected arrow movement must still yield.","fact_ids":["sec14-F09","sec14-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u02-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Arrows recap","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-R01","sec14-F09","sec14-F10","sec14-R03","sec14-F11","sec14-R02","sec14-F12","sec14-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Green arrow: protected; U-turns yield to rights.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-R01","sec14-F09","sec14-F10","sec14-R03","sec14-F11","sec14-R02","sec14-F12","sec14-F13"]},{"text":"Red arrow: no turn that way.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-R01","sec14-F09","sec14-F10","sec14-R03","sec14-F11","sec14-R02","sec14-F12","sec14-F13"]},{"text":"Yellow arrow: protection ending.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-R01","sec14-F09","sec14-F10","sec14-R03","sec14-F11","sec14-R02","sec14-F12","sec14-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"To finish, a green arrow gives a protected movement in the direction it points, entered carefully, and when a U-turn and an opposing right turn both have green arrows, the U-turning driver yields. A circular green turn, by contrast, must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. A red arrow stops turns in its direction, unlike a circular red that allows a right after a full stop unless signed. A yellow arrow warns that the protected phase is ending. When no arrow is lit, circular lights control everyone; when both show, arrows control turns and circles control through traffic.","fact_ids":["sec14-F08","sec14-R01","sec14-F09","sec14-F10","sec14-R03","sec14-F11","sec14-R02","sec14-F12","sec14-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec14-u03","module_id":"sec14-m03","objective_ids":["sec14-u03"],"title":{"text":"Dark and flashing signals","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F15","sec14-R06"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The handbook says a dark or malfunctioning signal is treated as an all-way stop, unless someone or something else is controlling traffic.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F15"]},{"text":"Flashing red and flashing yellow each match a familiar sign.","fact_ids":["sec14-F16","sec14-F17"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Jordan reaches an intersection after a storm and finds the traffic signal completely dark, with no officer present.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14"]},"reasoning":{"text":"At a signal that is dark or malfunctioning, treat the intersection as if every approach had a stop sign.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-R06"]},"result":{"text":"Jordan stops, takes turns with the other drivers, and proceeds when it is safe.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: driving straight through a dark signal on the main road as if it were green.","fact_ids":["sec14-R06"]},"correction":{"text":"A dark or broken signal means an all-way stop, unless an officer is directing traffic or another device is working.","fact_ids":["sec14-R06","sec14-F14","sec14-F15"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Dark signal, all-way stop.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Jordan finds a dark traffic signal and no officer. How should Jordan treat the intersection?","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-R06"]},"answer":{"text":"As if every approach had a stop sign.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14"]},"rationale":{"text":"A dark signal becomes an all-way stop unless an officer or another working device is controlling traffic.","fact_ids":["sec14-R06","sec14-F15"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec14-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"When signals change behavior","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F16","sec14-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Dark or broken signals.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F16","sec14-F17"]},{"text":"Flashing red.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F16","sec14-F17"]},{"text":"Flashing yellow.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F16","sec14-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers signals that are not showing their normal steady cycle. You will review what to do when a signal is dark or malfunctioning, the situations where that rule does not apply, and what flashing red and flashing yellow lights mean. The handbook ties each of these to a familiar sign, which makes them easier to remember: a dark signal becomes an all-way stop, a flashing red works like a stop sign, and a flashing yellow works like a warning sign. Practice questions often mix flashing red and flashing yellow, so keep them separate.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F16","sec14-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Dark or broken signals","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Treat it as an all-way stop.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F15"]},{"text":"Unless an officer directs traffic.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F15"]},{"text":"Or another control device is working.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"At a signal that is dark or malfunctioning, treat the intersection as if every approach had a stop sign. The all-way-stop rule for a broken signal does not apply when an officer or other authorized person directs traffic, or when another control device is working. So a dark signal does not give anyone the right of way by default. Every driver stops, as at a four-way stop. If an officer is directing traffic, you follow the officer. If another control device is working, you follow that device instead. When neither an officer nor another working device controls traffic, every approach stops.","fact_ids":["sec14-F14","sec14-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u03-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Dark does not mean go","fact_ids":["sec14-R06","sec14-F14","sec14-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Dark signal: all-way stop.","fact_ids":["sec14-R06","sec14-F14","sec14-F15"]},{"text":"Officer or another device: follow it.","fact_ids":["sec14-R06","sec14-F14","sec14-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some drivers on the main road keep going through a dark signal as if it were still green. The handbook says otherwise. A dark or broken traffic signal means an all-way stop, unless an officer is directing traffic or another device is working. On practice questions, an option that gives the main road priority at a dark signal is wrong. Ask two questions: is an officer or other authorized person directing traffic, and is another control device working? If neither, every approach stops, as though each had a stop sign.","fact_ids":["sec14-R06","sec14-F14","sec14-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec14-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Flashing red and flashing yellow","fact_ids":["sec14-F16","sec14-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Flashing red: same as a stop sign.","fact_ids":["sec14-F16","sec14-F17"]},{"text":"Flashing yellow: same as a warning sign.","fact_ids":["sec14-F16","sec14-F17"]},{"text":"Slow down and go on with caution.","fact_ids":["sec14-F16","sec14-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop and wait until you can enter without interfering with approaching traffic. A flashing yellow light means the same as a warning sign: slow down and go on with caution.
